title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-03-04
content:
Perf benchmarking sync - 2026-03-04

Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Miguel Alvarez, Sofia Kim

Agenda:
- Quick recap of last week's runs
- Investigate p50/p95 latency regression for long sequences on A100
- Validate throughput numbers after recent KV-cache changes
- Assign action items / next conformance runs

Summary:
We observed a measurable latency regression after merging PR #452 (KV cache refactor) that surfaced in yesterday's nightly perf job. The regression is most pronounced for long-context workloads (1k+ tokens) on A100 instances: p50 latency up ~12% and p95 up ~18% vs baseline (baseline = 2026-02-25 run). Short sequences (<128 tokens) unaffected. Throughput (tokens/sec) shows a ~7% drop at high concurrency (concurrency=32) for the same workloads.

Environment / baseline details:
- Model: rw-7b-v1 (fp16), same checkpoints across runs
- Hardware: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 8.7, NVIDIA driver 535.xx
- Serving runtime image: serving-runtime:2026-02-28 (baseline) vs serving-runtime:2026-03-02 (post-PR452)
- Test harness: perf-suite v0.9.2 (Jenkins job: perf-run-2026-03-04)
- Workloads: short-chat (32 tokens), med (256 tokens), long-context (1024 tokens)
- Batching config: dynamic batching enabled, max_batch_size=64, batching window=5ms

Observed numbers (representative):
- Baseline (2026-02-25) long-context, concurrency=16: p50=320ms, p95=560ms, throughput=7200 tokens/s
- Current (2026-03-04) long-context, concurrency=16: p50=358ms (+11.9%), p95=662ms (+18.2%), throughput=6700 tokens/s (-6.9%)
- Short-chat (concurrency=64): no statistically significant change (p50 ~18ms)

Initial triage notes:
- Regression correlates with PR #452 (KV cache refactor) which changed eviction heuristics and added an LRU compaction pass. Suspected contention in KV cache hot-path under long sequences where KV cache hits are frequent and compaction runs may compete for locks.
- Timeline: PR #452 merged 2026-03-01, nightly perf on 2026-03-02 showed small variance, full regression reproduced in controlled perf-run on 2026-03-03.
- Reproducer steps: run perf-suite with --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 16 --model rw-7b-v1 against serving-runtime:2026-03-02 image. See Jenkins job log for exact run commands.

Tests run this morning:
- Disabled LRU compaction via env var KV_CACHE_COMPACTION_ENABLED=false and reran long-context suite. Result: p50 dropped back to 326ms (within 2% of baseline) and throughput recovered to ~7100 tokens/s. Suggests compaction pass is the culprit.
- Run with serialized compaction (single compaction thread) produced intermediate numbers (p50~340ms) - indicates compaction concurrency amplifies impact.
- Additional run that pinned compaction to low-priority cgroups (niceness) reduced p95 tail but did not fully restore baseline.

Hypotheses:
1) Compaction runs are acquiring global locks / blocking inference threads during large KV cache operations for long sequences where many KV entries are inserted/evicted.
2) New eviction heuristics cause more frequent compaction cycles for workloads with wide attention windows (1k tokens).
3) Memory allocator interaction: compaction triggers large free/alloc patterns that increase latency spikes due to allocator behavior on A100 instance kernels.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: Open an instrumented build that logs compaction start/end times and lock hold durations. Add histograms for compaction runtime. Target: PR with logs by 2026-03-06. (blocked on test infra access)
- Liam: Prototype a non-blocking compaction strategy (incremental compaction) in a feature branch and run perf comparisons. ETA: initial branch by 2026-03-09.
- Priya: Run allocator-focused experiments (jemalloc vs tcmalloc) on perf cluster to see allocator impact on tail latency. Capture callstacks / flame graphs for compaction periods. ETA: 2026-03-07.
- Miguel: Roll back PR #452 in a canary image and run full perf suite against canary to validate that rollback restores baseline across all workloads. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- Sofia: Update perf-run harness to add compaction-aware metrics and alert thresholds so the nightly job surfaces this earlier. ETA: 2026-03-06.

Risks and mitigation:
- Rolling back PR #452 will remove other KV-cache improvements (memory usage and some throughput wins on mid-length sequences). We need to quantify the tradeoffs before reverting in production.
- Non-blocking compaction may be complex; the incremental approach must preserve correctness (no lost KV entries). Prioritize correctness tests and add unit/integration coverage.

Follow-ups planned for next sync:
- Share compaction telemetry (Aisha) and allocator experiment results (Priya)
- Review Liam's incremental compaction prototype if perf shows promise
- Decide on temporary mitigation (disable compaction by default for long-context jobs) to be applied to hosted nightly runs
- Re-run full perf suite on canary rollback image and post results to Confluence page

Notes / loose threads:
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/452 (KV cache refactor)
- Jira ticket: JIRA-INF-789 created to track the regression and root-cause activities
- Perf run logs: jenkin-job/serving-runtime/perf-run-2026-03-04 (contains raw logs and flame graphs)

Meeting adjourned - next sync: 2026-03-06 10:00 PT (standup channel #eng-serving-runtime, calendar invite sent)

Raw experiment commands (for reproducibility):
- ./perf-suite run --model rw-7b-v1 --image serving-runtime:2026-03-02 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 16 --batching dynamic --out logs/run-2026-03-04-long.txt
- export KV_CACHE_COMPACTION_ENABLED=false; ./perf-suite run --model rw-7b-v1 --image serving-runtime:2026-03-02 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 16 --out logs/run-2026-03-04-nocompaction.txt
- jemalloc test: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libjemalloc.so ./perf-suite run --... (see Jenkins job for full flags)

If anyone has extra reproducer scripts or captured flame graphs, drop them in the linked Jenkins job artefacts and ping in #eng-serving-runtime.
